scope.method: Read-only inspection of the build source, generated HTML, JavaScript, CSS, research JSON, media manifest and README; focused parsing of local references, IDs, text preservation and attribution. No browser use or site edits.
excluded: Browser and visual QA, owned by the root agent
Fresh external-link availability or video playback verification
Independent re-verification of external image licences, covered by the media/source review
The known phone QA fixture as a release asset

checks.evidence: All local href, src and poster targets from index.html and Timeline-Reader.html resolve. All local fragment targets resolve. CSS contains no url() resource references requiring resolution.

The plain reading edition contains all 60 event IDs exactly once, with the complete final summaries and notes. Its ./ return link resolves to the audiovisual index. It has no scripts, audio, video or iframe elements.
All data-event-link attributes target existing milestone IDs and match their href fragments. Every related_event_ids relationship in the final data is rendered in its originating event card.

All final event summaries and date notes are present in both HTML editions. All seven researched introductions are visible in the main edition. build_site.py replaces its initial chapter-intro defaults with chapters.json before rendering. The fifteen studio albums and 35 flagged audiovisual events match the README.

floyd.js creates a youtube-nocookie iframe only in the video-selection path invoked by a visitor's open/previous/next button. All ten manifest YouTube IDs satisfy the expected eleven-character format. The URL sets autoplay=0; iframe permissions omit autoplay. Closing the dialog removes the iframe. No fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, speechSynthesis, Audio constructor or programmatic play call appears in floyd.js. The manifest's thumbnail URLs are data only and are not emitted as initial image requests.

The release contains no narration audio files or narration playback control. README explicitly says narration was unavailable and no narration audio is included or claimed. It also records that successful embedded video playback was not verified in the shared browser, preserving that limitation instead of claiming playback success.

Every photograph's local WebP exists and matches its manifest hash and byte count. Each rendered figure carries its creator, capture date and stated licence, with source and licence links. Credits and README preserve the ShareAlike wording and change notice. Context photographs retain later capture dates; the Toronto metadata is qualified and is not used as evidence for the Ottawa tour opening. The generated abstract cover is labelled as AI-generated and is separate from the historical photographs.

The site and Reader state the 15 November 2026 research cutoff. 8-Tracks is dated 5 June 2026 with market variation in notes. Echoes restoration retains October 2026 month precision and the source discrepancy note. The final milestone is dated 5 November 2026 and marked as an announcement. The dedicated future-release section says Animals 50 is scheduled for 22 January 2027 and that the edition closes before release. Neither edition claims the 2027 release has already happened.

build_site.py consumes the final timeline and chapter research, renders all milestones, builds links from verified IDs, writes the two research JSON files, and serializes the same media manifest used by the player. Main HTML text is escaped; the serialized manifest escapes closing-tag sequences. The generated result matches the inspected research and manifest.

known_release_cleanup.action: Remove the phone QA fixture before publishing, as already planned by the root agent.

limitations: Static review cannot establish successful playback, live provider availability, deployed routing or visual layout.
Licence integration was checked against the reviewed manifest; the external rights claims were not re-audited in this focused pass.
Changes after this snapshot are outside the review, apart from the already planned QA-fixture removal.
